PullRequest.Title: sessions: Track accepted Dev Container sample selections
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

Refs #339581. Follow-up to #339067.

## Summary

Adds `devContainerSampleSelected` telemetry after an accepted user selection in the Agents workspace picker.

- The only event-specific payload is `sampleId`, typed from the built-in catalog: `go`, `dotnet`, `node`, `php`, `python`, or `rust`.
- Uses the common accepted-selection path for submenu entries, filtered results, and recent sample workspaces.
- Does not emit for programmatic restoration/selection, ordinary folders, malformed sample URIs, unavailable providers, or declined/failed/superseded selections.
- Leaves `newChatPickerClosed` and its workspace privacy filtering unchanged.
- Classifies the catalog ID as `SystemMetaData` / `FeatureInsight`, owned by `chrmarti`. No paths, repository URLs, labels, prompts, or file contents are included in the new payload.

This measures sample selection, not provisioning success or first-prompt usage. It is not an experiment trigger, since users without the sample menu cannot select a sample.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` - passed with zero compilation errors after restoring the checkout's declared/locked dependencies.
- `node .\build\hygiene.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\browser\sessionWorkspacePicker.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\sessionWorkspacePicker.test.ts` - passed.
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\sessionWorkspacePicker.test.ts --grep 'WorkspacePicker - Dev Container sample telemetry' --reporter dot` - 8 passed.
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\sessionWorkspacePicker.test.ts --reporter dot` - all 147 tests passed.
- `git diff --cached --check` - passed.

The Electron test launcher could not replace the older runtime while Code OSS held it open; the repository's Chromium runner was used instead. No dependency manifests or lockfiles changed.

## How to test

1. Enable Dev Container samples and their prerequisites in the Agents window.
2. Pick a sample from the submenu, filtered results, or a recent sample entry.
3. In telemetry output, verify one `devContainerSampleSelected` event with only the corresponding catalog `sampleId` as its event-specific payload.
4. Open/dismiss the picker or select an ordinary folder; verify no sample-selection event is emitted.
5. Sending a prompt is not required for this event.

Scenarios.Scenario: User accepts a Dev Container sample from the submenu, filtered results, or a recent-workspace entry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user selection enters _dispatchPickerItem, emits the pre-existing newChatPickerClosed event, optionally connects the provider, awaits selection validation, commits the folder selection, performs a fixed-catalog sample lookup, and synchronously prepares one new telemetry event before the dispatch promise resolves. Desktop/remote telemetry transport and web SDK delivery are fire-and-forget and are not awaited; the picker is hidden immediately by the selection delegate.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optional on-demand provider connection before workspace acceptance
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one connection attempt for the selected provider, only when disconnected and connectable; zero for the local sample provider or an already-connected provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider connection attempt was awaited before accepting the selected workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited and potentially dominant when needed, but unchanged by this PR and completed before the added lookup/event.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existence check for file-scheme workspace selections
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one exists call per selected local file URI; Dev Container sample URIs use a distinct scheme, so this is zero for the sample-selection scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same existence check occurred before accepting local file workspaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited for ordinary local folders, but not reached as filesystem I/O for sample URIs and unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Desktop telemetry appender channel enqueue for devContainerSampleSelected
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one new IPC call per accepted sample when desktop telemetry is enabled; no call when telemetry is disabled. The scenario already emits one separate newChatPickerClosed telemetry event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An accepted selection emitted newChatPickerClosed, but did not emit this second sample-specific telemetry call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Payload cleaning and channel enqueue are synchronous and bounded; delivery is fire-and-forget and not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Web or remote telemetry appender enqueue/delivery for devContainerSampleSelected
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one small event per accepted sample when usage telemetry is enabled, forwarded through one configured transport plus the existing log appender.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same accepted selection had no sample-specific event, although it already emitted newChatPickerClosed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The appender queues/tracks the event without awaiting network completion; only bounded preparation is on the selection path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected workspace URI per user action. findDevContainerSample scans at most the six built-in catalog entries, and the diff emits exactly one small event for an accepted sample; there is no workspace-, repository-, or result-list-sized loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Selection generations suppress accepted superseded async selections. Each accepted user action can enqueue one telemetry append; the diff does not launch a collection burst or add parallel provider operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The six-entry catalog lookup needs no cache. If experiment properties are not ready, telemetry uses the existing globally capped pending-event buffer; once warm it immediately forwards to configured appenders. Provider connection status is reused on warm selections. The diff adds no cache keys, misses, negative-cache state, or invalidation lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line, fixed six-element lookup, accepted-selection call path, telemetry service cleaning, configured appenders, and fire-and-forget IPC/network behavior were all traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timing measurement is available for telemetry cleaning/channel enqueue, and configured appenders vary by desktop/web/remote environment. The payload and event cardinality are fixed and tiny, so this uncertainty does not establish a realistic regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The PR intentionally adds one bounded telemetry event to a low-frequency accepted user action; it neither fans out with a collection nor awaits transport, and the fixed lookup cannot grow with user data.

Scenarios.Scenario: User selects an ordinary folder or a malformed sample URI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the unchanged provider-connect and selection-validation steps, the diff calls findDevContainerSample. Ordinary schemes fail the initial scheme test; malformed sample-scheme URIs either fail authority/query/fragment checks or scan the six-entry catalog. No new telemetry append occurs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optional provider connection or custom canSelectWorkspace validation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one provider connection/validation sequence for the single selected URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same connection and validation sequence occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited but entirely pre-existing; the added lookup runs only after it completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one exists call for one file-scheme folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same existence check occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited and unchanged; no telemetry boundary is added for the ordinary or malformed URI.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One URI per accepted user selection; lookup cost is constant and capped at six comparisons regardless of workspace history or picker result count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One lookup per accepted dispatch. Superseded asynchronous selections are rejected by the existing generation checks before reaching the added lookup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is needed or introduced because the lookup's maximum cardinality is six. Existing provider connection state remains the only warm-path distinction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: helper guards and the fixed catalog were inspected, and the changed telemetry branch is not entered for these inputs.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Custom provider validation duration is provider-specific, but it is unchanged and unrelated to the constant-time added lookup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The only new work is a bounded URI check/fixed six-entry scan with no new IPC, filesystem, or network operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workspace selection is restored programmatically, unavailable, declined, failed, or superseded
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Programmatic restoration uses setSelectedWorkspace rather than _dispatchPickerItem. Unavailable providers return before validation; declined/failed/superseded asynchronous selections return or throw before the changed lines. Therefore neither the new catalog lookup nor the new telemetry event runs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Possible pre-existing provider connection or selection validation before a declined/failed/superseded outcome
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one sequence for the attempted selection; zero for programmatic restoration and immediately unavailable providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical connection/validation behavior, with no sample-specific telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: May be awaited for an attempted selection, but unchanged by the diff; rejection occurs before the new telemetry boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One attempted selection; effective new-work cardinality is zero for all listed outcomes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing selection generation invalidates superseded attempts. The diff adds no queued, concurrent, or retained work on these paths.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache access or telemetry buffering occurs because the changed branch is not reached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: generation and early-return guards precede the changed lines, and tests exercise each non-emitting outcome.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific connection/validation cost is not measured, but the PR introduces no work on these rejected or restoration paths.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression because all newly added runtime work is bypassed.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. The sole production change adds a fixed six-entry lookup and one small, non-awaited telemetry append after a rare accepted sample selection. Existing provider, filesystem, IPC, and network boundaries were compared before/after; no scaling, burst, retention, eager-work, or critical-path regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
